text:
alex: quick heads-up — seeing steady RSS growth on streaming-chat when the tool-loop is enabled. reproducer: local heavy-tool run, ~12h soak. kv_cache_resident_bytes keeps creeping up even though eviction counters tick.

maria: can you share the top-line metrics and a short pprof/heap sample? is eviction happening but pages not returned to OS?

alex: pasting the small excerpt from /metrics and jemalloc snapshot we took:

```
kv_cache_resident_bytes 734003200
kv_cache_evictions_total 238
kv_slot_allocated 89231
kv_slot_free 1284
jemalloc.active 754321920
jemalloc.allocated 489123456
jemalloc.metadata 2097152
```

alex: interestingly total mallocs don't grow much — allocated is stable — but "active" keeps drifting up. suggests fragmentation or unreturned pages.

raj: my first guess is fragmentation from mixed allocation sizes in KV slots. tool loops create a lot of short-lived small keys and occasional large blobs, which can fragment arenas. what allocator settings are you running (per-thread arenas, decay, etc.)?

alex: default jemalloc config from our docker image. not using tight decay. will try `MALLOC_CONF=purge:decay,lg_chunk:21` and rerun.

taylor: also consider whether our KV page allocator does small-slab suballocation that prevents coalescing. if the index keeps alternate dense/sparse pages we can get holes that avoid reuse.

ops-bot: alert: kv_cache_resident_growth_rate high — trigger=200MB/hr on prod/streaming-chat (fyi)

maria: can you capture `malloc_stats_print` and a `jeprof` before/after? also expose `kv.slot.alloc_count` and `kv.slot.free_count` for a run.

alex: started a short 3h soak with `MALLOC_CONF=purge:decay,lg_chunk:20` and enabled additional metrics. reproduce command:

```
./run-local --mode=streaming --tool-loop=heavy --duration=3h --metrics=prometheus
curl http://localhost:9090/metrics | grep kv_
```

alex: early results — RSS slope reduced ~40% vs baseline for first 2h, but slow drift remains. fragmentation ratio (jemalloc.active/jemalloc.allocated) ~1.54 => ~35% overhead.

raj: ok that indicates fragmentation but not a leak. next hypothesis: our KV allocator's free-list segmentation prevents slot reuse across different size classes because we embed size-class into slot headers; big->small reuse disabled. check `kv.slot_size_classes` and `kv.reuse_threshold`.

taylor: i can try toggling `--kv-allow-reuse-crossclass=true` in a canary to see if reuse helps. downside: needs safe checks for stale pointers; may increase CPU from more checks.

maria: also try background compaction: `kv.compact()` that coalesces adjacent free pages into larger runs. do it incrementally to avoid pauses. set schedule to every 30m and track RSS.

alex: enabled incremental compaction with `--kv-compact-increment=1MB/s` and the decay config. running 24h soak now. will post heap diff after 24h.

ops-bot: deploy job #3382 succeeded (canary with kv-compact, env=MALLOC_CONF applied)

alex: preliminary 6h snapshot: RSS slope now ~8MB/hr (was ~30MB/hr baseline). eviction count unchanged. compaction introduced tiny CPU bump (~2%) but no pause spikes in traces.

raj: promising. still curious about long-tail sessions: do we see slot residency skew? run query: `sum by (slot_size) (kv.slot_resident_bytes)` to see if a particular size bin holds most residual.

maria: also capture `mallctl` arena stats and `arenas.lextents.*` to see if extents leaked (unreleased mmap'd pages). if extents stay allocated, compaction won't return to OS unless we madvise or purge.

taylor: if extents persist, we should try `mallctl` purge and test aggressive decay on a test node. if that helps, we can add periodic `jemalloc_purge()` triggered after compaction iterations.

alex: capturing those next. tl;dr so far: combination of jemalloc decay tuning + incremental KV compaction reduced growth by ~70% across experiments. remaining drift likely due to cross-class fragmentation and reserved extents.

maria: next steps: 1) run 48h soak with canary flags, 2) collect full heap dump and jeprof at start/mid/end, 3) add metric `kv.compaction_runs_total` and `kv.purge_runs_total` so we can correlate.

raj: i'm going to prototype a safe cross-class reuse path (low-risk build) and run microbenchmarks to ensure no correctness regression.

taylor: I'll add a dashboard tile for `jemalloc.active` and `kv.slot_frag_pct` and hook an alert at 250MB/hr just until we stabilize.

alex: thanks everyone — opening ENG-1234 with the experiment results and links to the canary runs. will paste artifacts once 48h completes. :thumbsup:
